stemBlocks.value: Grade 11 students were surveyed about the job sector they are most likely to seek employment in. On the pie chart the sectors are: Health care 90° (marked as a right angle), ICT 67.5°, Agriculture 40.5°, Government 4p°, Education 3p° and Real estate 2p°. Find the value of p (and hence the angle of each remaining sector).
Think first: The right-angle mark on the health care sector is data: it tells you that sector is 90°.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p228-q12 from workbook page 228.

solutionSteps.instruction: Write down all six sector angles, using 90° for the right-angled health care sector.

contentBlocks.value: Result: Six angles, three of them in terms of p

solutionSteps.instruction: Set the sum of the angles equal to a whole turn.
Substitute back to check the six angles total 360°.

strategyBlocks.value: Add all six sector angles, set the sum equal to 360°, and solve the resulting linear equation for p.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: p = 18, giving Government = 72°, Education = 54° and Real estate = 36° (with Health care 90°, ICT 67.5° and Agriculture 40.5°).

whyThisWorks.value: The sectors of a pie chart meet at the centre, so their angles are angles at a point and must total exactly 360°. Writing three unknown sectors as multiples of the same letter turns that fact into a single linear equation, and the right-angle symbol supplies the sixth angle without it needing to be stated in words.

commonErrors.misconception: Ignoring the right-angle mark and leaving the health care sector as an unknown.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Ignoring the right-angle mark and leaving the health care sector as an unknown.
